examples.en: The weather is so dreary that I don't want to go outside.
Even though it's daytime, the sky is dark and gloomy.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 밤에는 골목이 더 음산해 보여요.
examples.en: On rainy nights the alley looks even more eerie.
That movie had a dismal atmosphere.

examples.ko: 음산한 바람이 불더니 갑자기 비가 쏟아졌어요.
examples.en: A gloomy wind blew, and then suddenly the rain poured down.

examples.ko: 그 집은 낮에는 별로 음산하지 않아요.
examples.en: That house doesn't feel very gloomy during the day.

explain: '으스스하다'와 비슷하지만 '음산하다'는 날씨나 분위기가 어둡고 쓸쓸해서 기분이 가라앉을 때 주로 써요. '음산한 날씨', '음산한 분위기'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '으스스하다'나 '우중충하다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '으스스하다' (eerie), but '음산하다' is mainly used when the weather or atmosphere is dark and lonely and brings your mood down. It often appears before a noun, as in '음산한 날씨' or '음산한 분위기'. In everyday talk people also say '으스스하다' or '우중충하다'.

examples.ko: 음성적 거래를 하는 곳이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of places doing underground deals is growing.
Exchanging money secretly is illegal.

examples.ko: 그 시장은 음성적이어서 규모를 알기 어려워요.
examples.en: That market is underground, so it's hard to know its size.
It is hard to pay taxes on hidden income.
Deals that used to be hidden are now done in the open.

examples.ko: 일을 음성적이지 않게 투명하게 처리해야 해요.
examples.en: You should handle the work transparently, not secretly.

explain: 뉴스에서 '음성적 거래', '음성적 수입'처럼 법이나 제도 밖에서 몰래 이루어지는 일에 많이 써요. 숨어 있던 것을 드러내서 공개하는 것은 '양성화'라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. '음성적인', '음성적으로'처럼 활용해서 써요.
explain_en: In the news it is used for things done secretly outside the law or the system, as in '음성적 거래' (underground dealing) or '음성적 수입' (hidden income). Its counterpart is '양성화', which means bringing something hidden into the open. It also appears as '음성적인' or '음성적으로'.

examples.en: The basement is damp, so mold has formed.

examples.ko: 그 방은 햇빛이 안 들어서 음습해요.
examples.en: That room gets no sunlight, so it's dank.
Walking through the damp, dark alley was a little scary.
During the rainy season the inside of the house feels clammy.
I open the windows often so it doesn't get damp.
This house is old, so it was always damp.

explain: '축축하다'는 단순히 젖어 있는 느낌이지만, '음습하다'는 어둡고 눅눅해서 기분이 개운하지 않은 느낌까지 담겨 있어요. 지하실이나 골목, 오래된 방처럼 장소에 주로 써요.
explain_en: '축축하다' just means wet or moist, while '음습하다' also carries a dark, clammy and slightly unpleasant feeling. It is mostly used for places such as basements, alleys and old rooms.

examples.en: That movie has a gloomy mood overall.
His expression looks gloomy these days.
Listening to the melancholy music brought my mood down.
On rainy days my heart gets gloomy.
The novel's atmosphere was so gloomy that it was hard to read.

examples.ko: 음울하지 않은 밝은 노래를 틀어 주세요.
examples.en: Please play a bright song that isn't gloomy.

explain: '우울하다'와 비슷하지만, 사람의 기분은 보통 '우울하다'라고 말해요. '음울하다'는 분위기, 음악, 날씨, 색깔처럼 어둡고 가라앉은 느낌에 더 잘 어울려요. 책이나 영화 이야기에서 자주 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is close to '우울하다' (depressed), but people usually describe their own mood with '우울하다'. '음울하다' fits better for a dark, subdued feel in an atmosphere, music, weather or color. You often meet it when people talk about books and movies.

examples.en: The alley is dark, so it looks sinister.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말이 없고 좀 음침해요.
examples.en: That person is quiet and a bit creepy.

examples.ko: 음침한 분위기의 카페라서 오래 못 있었어요.
examples.en: The café had a gloomy vibe, so I couldn't stay long.
The abandoned house felt sinister even in the daytime.

examples.ko: 음침하게 웃지 말고 그냥 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't smile creepily, just tell me.
The hallway with the lights off is gloomy and scary.

explain: 어둡고 으스스한 장소에도 쓰고, 말이 없고 속을 알 수 없는 사람에게도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 부정적인 말이에요. '음흉하다'는 나쁜 속셈이 있다는 느낌이고, '음침하다'는 어둡고 기분 나쁜 분위기가 중심이에요.
explain_en: It is used both for dark, creepy places and for quiet people whose thoughts are hard to read. Said about a person, it is negative. '음흉하다' suggests a hidden bad intention, while '음침하다' is mostly about a dark, unpleasant feel.

examples.en: A rumor going around was meant to smear a rival.
He slandered his coworker with lies.

examples.ko: 저를 음해하려는 사람이 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think there is someone trying to slander me.

examples.ko: 남을 음해해서 얻는 이익은 오래가지 않아요.
examples.en: Gains from slandering others don't last long.

examples.ko: 누가 회사 대표를 음해했는지 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are investigating who slandered the company head.
Don't slander people carelessly, check the facts first.

explain: '험담하다'는 뒤에서 흉을 보는 정도지만, '음해하다'는 몰래 거짓말이나 나쁜 계획으로 남을 곤란하게 만든다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스나 회사, 정치 이야기에서 자주 나오고 일상 대화에서는 조금 무거운 말이에요.
explain_en: '험담하다' is just bad-mouthing someone behind their back, but '음해하다' strongly suggests secretly using lies or schemes to bring someone down. It appears in news, workplace and political stories, and sounds rather heavy in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 잘 웃지만 속은 음흉해요.
examples.en: He smiles a lot, but he is sly inside.

examples.ko: 음흉한 계획을 세운 사람이 누군지 알아냈어요.
examples.en: We found out who made the sneaky plan.
Why are you smiling so slyly?

examples.ko: 겉모습은 착해 보여도 음흉할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Someone may look nice and still be cunning.

examples.ko: 이야기 속 악당은 음흉해서 아무도 믿지 않아요.
examples.en: The villain in the story is so cunning that nobody trusts him.
I like people who are honest, not sly.

explain: 겉으로는 얌전하거나 친절한데 속으로 나쁜 생각을 숨기고 있을 때 써요. 속셈이 있어 보이는 웃음이나 눈빛에 특히 잘 어울려요. '음침하다'는 어두운 분위기가 중심이고, '음흉하다'는 숨은 속셈이 중심이에요.
explain_en: Use it when someone looks calm or kind outside but hides bad thoughts inside. It suits a smile or a look that seems to hide a scheme. '음침하다' is mainly about a dark feel, while '음흉하다' is about a hidden intention.

examples.en: The lawmaker pleaded with tears in front of the public.
Begging doesn't necessarily solve the problem.

examples.ko: 사장님께 읍소하며 한 번만 기회를 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I pleaded with the boss and asked for just one more chance.
The company sent customers a letter of earnest appeal.

examples.ko: 읍소해도 이미 마음이 떠난 사람들은 돌아오지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if you plead, people who have already left in heart won't come back.

examples.ko: 그는 판사에게 한 번만 봐 달라고 읍소하려고 해요.
examples.en: He is going to beg the judge to let him off just once.

explain: 눈물을 흘릴 만큼 간절하게 호소한다는 느낌이라서 뉴스에서 정치인이나 기업이 국민, 고객에게 사과하고 부탁할 때 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '사정하다', '빌다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of appealing so earnestly that tears may come, so in the news it often appears when politicians or companies apologize and ask for understanding. In daily talk people more often say '사정하다' or '빌다'.

examples.en: When water vapor touches cold glass, it condenses.
Water droplets condensed on the outside of the cold cup.

examples.ko: 공기 중의 수증기가 응결하여 구름이 돼요.
examples.en: Water vapor in the air condenses and becomes clouds.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 창문 안쪽에 수증기가 응결하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In winter, water vapor easily condenses on the inside of the window.

examples.ko: 수증기가 응결하면 벽에 곰팡이가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If vapor condenses, mold can grow on the walls.
Please wipe off the condensed water drops with a towel.

explain: 과학 수업에서는 기체가 액체로 변하는 것을 말하고, 생활에서는 찬 컵이나 창문에 물방울이 맺히는 일에 써요. 집 벽이나 창문에 생기는 물방울은 '결로'라고도 해요.
explain_en: In science class it means a gas turning into a liquid, and in daily life it covers water drops forming on a cold cup or a window. Drops that form on walls or windows at home are also called '결로'.

examples.en: The department head gladly agreed to my request.
After thinking for a long time, he agreed to the marriage.
Check the conditions before you accept the offer.

examples.ko: 부모님이 응낙하시면 여행을 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If my parents agree, I can go on the trip.

examples.ko: 그녀는 바로 응낙하지 않고 생각해 보겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: She didn't agree right away and said she would think about it.

examples.ko: 상대가 응낙해서 계약을 맺을 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The other side agreed, so we were able to sign the contract.

explain: 부탁이나 제안을 받아들인다는 격식 있는 말이에요. 말할 때는 보통 '허락하다', '승낙하다', '받아들이다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 글이나 이야기 속에서 이 말을 볼 수 있어요. 윗사람이 허락할 때는 '응낙하시다'처럼 높여요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for accepting a request or proposal. In speech people usually say '허락하다', '승낙하다' or '받아들이다', and you are more likely to see this word in writing or stories. When a superior agrees, you honor them as '응낙하시다'.

examples.en: In summer it's good to rest in the shade.
The snow in the shady spots hasn't melted yet.

examples.ko: 빨래를 응달에 널면 잘 안 말라요.
examples.en: If you hang laundry in the shade, it doesn't dry well.

examples.ko: 이 화분은 응달도 괜찮아서 키우기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This plant is fine even in the shade, so it's easy to grow.
It's a shady spot, so it's a bit cold even in the daytime.

examples.ko: 우리 집 뒤쪽은 응달이라 겨울에 얼음이 많아요.
examples.en: The back of our house is in shadow, so there is a lot of ice in winter.

explain: '그늘'은 나무나 건물 때문에 생긴 어두운 자리이고, '응달'은 방향 때문에 해가 잘 들지 않는 곳이에요. 반대말은 햇볕이 잘 드는 '양달'이에요. 한자어로는 '음지'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '그늘' is a dark spot made by a tree or a building, while '응달' is a place that gets little sun because of the direction it faces. The opposite is '양달', a sunny spot. The Sino-Korean word '음지' means the same.

examples.ko: 산 북쪽은 응달져서 눈이 늦게 녹아요.
examples.en: The north side of the mountain is in shade, so the snow melts late.
Moss grows a lot in shady places.

examples.ko: 집 앞이 응달지면 겨울에 길이 얼기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If the front of your house is shady, the road freezes easily in winter.
This room is shaded by the building.

examples.ko: 응달지지 않은 쪽에 화분을 놓아 주세요.
examples.en: Please put the pot on the side that isn't shady.
It's a road between buildings, so it's always in shade.

explain: '응달진 곳'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 써요. '응달지다'는 '응달진, 응달져요, 응달졌어요'로 활용해요. 반대로 해가 잘 드는 곳은 '볕이 잘 들다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It often appears before a noun, as in '응달진 곳' (a shady place). It conjugates as '응달진', '응달져요' and '응달졌어요'. For a place with plenty of sun, you say '볕이 잘 들다'.

examples.en: If you did something wrong, you should apologize, as is only right.

examples.ko: 일한 만큼 응당 보수를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: You should receive pay in proportion to the work you did.

examples.ko: 그건 응당 제가 해야 할 일이에요.
examples.en: That is something I ought to do, as a matter of course.
You made a promise, so you must keep it.
A parent naturally thinks of the child first.
Citizens ought to follow the law, as is only right.

explain: '당연히'와 비슷하지만 '응당'은 '마땅히 ~해야 한다'처럼 도리나 의무를 말할 때 써요. 뒤에 '-아야/어야 하다'가 자주 오고, 말할 때는 '당연히'나 '마땅히'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is like '당연히' (naturally), but '응당' is used when talking about duty or what is right, as in 'you should do this as is proper'. It is often followed by '-아야/어야 하다'. In speech, people more often say '당연히' or '마땅히'.

examples.en: The child acts spoiled with its mother.
The youngest acts very spoiled in front of Dad.

examples.ko: 그만 응석 부리고 혼자 해 보세요.
examples.en: Stop acting spoiled and try doing it on your own.
My younger sibling is both clingy and teary.

examples.ko: 응석만 부리지 말고 스스로 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just act spoiled, try doing it by yourself.

examples.ko: 아이의 응석은 다 받아 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't give in to all of a child's whining.

explain: 보통 '응석을 부리다', '응석을 받아 주다'처럼 짝으로 써요. '어리광'과 비슷하지만, 어른이 응석을 부리면 철이 없다는 느낌이 들 수 있어요. 가까운 사람에게 기대고 싶어서 하는 행동이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used in pairs like '응석을 부리다' (act spoiled) and '응석을 받아 주다' (indulge someone). It is close to '어리광', but when an adult does it, it can sound immature. It is behavior from wanting to lean on someone close.

examples.en: Our youngest is a spoiled baby.

examples.ko: 응석꾸러기 동생이 또 안아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: My clingy little sibling is asking to be held again.
Even though he's grown up, he acts like a spoiled child.
I was a spoiled child when I was little.
I try not to raise him to be spoiled.
That puppy is such a clingy little one.

explain: '-꾸러기'는 '장난꾸러기', '잠꾸러기'처럼 그런 버릇이 많은 사람을 가리켜요. 아이한테는 귀엽게 말할 수 있지만, 어른에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 강아지 같은 동물에게도 써요.
explain_en: The ending '-꾸러기' points to someone with a lot of a certain habit, as in '장난꾸러기' (prankster) or '잠꾸러기' (sleepyhead). It can sound cute for a child, but for an adult it feels teasing. It is also used for animals such as puppies.

examples.en: The baby started crying with a wail.
I heard a baby's cry from next door all night.

examples.ko: 응애 하는 울음소리가 병원에 울려 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A baby's wail echoed through the hospital.

examples.ko: 아기가 태어나자마자 응애 하고 크게 울었어요.
examples.en: The baby cried out loud as soon as it was born.

examples.ko: 조카는 배가 고프면 응애 하며 보채요.
examples.en: My nephew fusses with a wail when he is hungry.

examples.ko: 갑자기 응애 하는 소리에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a sudden baby's cry.

explain: 갓난아기가 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 보통 '응애응애'처럼 반복해서도 써요. 조금 큰 아이가 크게 우는 소리는 '앙앙', '엉엉'처럼 달리 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of a newborn baby crying. It is often repeated as '응애응애'. For a somewhat older child crying loudly, people use other sounds such as '앙앙' or '엉엉'.

en: have an unpleasant feeling; have an ill feeling

examples.en: I let out the feelings that had knotted up inside me.
An old misunderstanding has lodged in my heart.
My hurt feelings have hardened, so I don't want to talk to him.

examples.ko: 서운한 일은 응어리지지 않게 바로 말해요.
examples.en: I speak up about hurtful things right away so they don't fester.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 상처가 아직도 응어리져 있어요.
examples.en: The wound from my childhood is still knotted up inside.

examples.ko: 마음이 응어리지면 몸도 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your heart gets knotted up, your body can hurt too.

explain: 풀리지 않은 서운함이나 원망이 마음속에 단단하게 남아 있을 때 써요. '응어리를 풀다', '응어리가 풀리다'처럼 반대되는 짝말도 함께 알아 두세요. '응어리진 마음'처럼 꾸미는 모양으로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: Use it when unresolved hurt or resentment stays hard inside your heart. Learn its opposites too, such as '응어리를 풀다' and '응어리가 풀리다' (to release it). It is also common before a noun, as in '응어리진 마음'.

examples.en: The child is mumbling something to himself.
He was shy and murmured quietly.
Don't mumble, please speak up.
I heard someone mumbling in their sleep.
I did the dishes while humming a song under my breath.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 입안으로 응얼거려서 잘 못 알아들었어요.
examples.en: Grandpa mumbled inside his mouth, so I couldn't catch it well.

explain: 분명하지 않게 낮은 소리로 말하거나 노래할 때 써요. '중얼거리다'와 비슷하지만 입안에서 웅웅 울리는 듯한 느낌이 더 강해요. '웅얼거리다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it for speaking or singing in a low, unclear voice. It is similar to '중얼거리다' (mutter) but gives a stronger sense of sound humming inside the mouth. It can also be said as '웅얼거리다'.

examples.en: A reliable supporter came, and it gave me strength.
My friends came to the match as my cheering squad.

examples.ko: 팬들은 우리 팀의 가장 큰 응원군이에요.
examples.en: The fans are our team's biggest supporters.
The more supporters there are, the more energy I get.

examples.ko: 이번 일에는 응원군을 더 모아야 해요.
examples.en: For this job we need to gather more backup.
I had my family as supporters, so I didn't give up.

explain: 나를 응원해 주는 사람들이나, 힘들 때 도우러 와 주는 사람들을 가리켜요. '응원단'은 경기장에서 응원을 이끄는 단체이고, '응원군'은 힘이 되어 주는 사람이라는 느낌이 더 커요. '지원군'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to people who cheer for you or come to help when things are hard. '응원단' is a group that leads cheering at a stadium, while '응원군' leans more toward people who give you strength. It is sometimes used much like '지원군'.

examples.en: Our team is really cohesive.
We had a meal together to build more unity.
Cohesion doesn't appear overnight.
Their teamwork is good and their cohesion is impressive too.
The cohesive team won the championship in the end.

examples.ko: 그 동네는 주민들의 응집력으로 위기를 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: That neighborhood overcame the crisis thanks to its residents' unity.

explain: 사람들이 한마음으로 뭉치는 힘을 말하고, '응집력이 강하다/높다/약하다/떨어지다'처럼 써요. '단결력'과 비슷하지만 모임이나 팀이 얼마나 끈끈한지 그 상태를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 과학 시간에는 물질의 입자가 서로 뭉치는 힘을 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the force that holds people together as one, used like '응집력이 강하다/높다/약하다/떨어지다'. It is close to '단결력' but fits best when describing how tight-knit a group or team is. In science class it can also mean the force that holds particles of a substance together.
